Mansory Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 Is So Brown It Should Come With a Giant Waste Bag
19 photos
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory
It is usually the Maybach version of the Mercedes GLS that gets the spotlight in our news feed, but this time, it is all about its sporty sibling from the Affalterbach division. That would be the Mercedes-AMG GLS 63, by the way.
This particular full-size SUV has come directly from Mansory’s portfolio, and given the overall look, we wouldn’t have expected it to have been signed by a different tuner to be honest. That’s because it is definitely on the controversial side of things, as the color choice makes it look questionable, to say the least, and the extras on the outside are not exactly head-turning for the reasons either, are they?
Nevertheless, beauty is indeed in the eyes of the beholder as they say, and while some may find this tuned Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 debatable, others would say that it is the absolute bomb, and if the latter category’s pockets are deep enough, then they would probably ask where they should sign, and how much does this thing cost. And guess what? It is not for sale. Mansory said this is a bespoke project, and it is likely a special commission.
The images you see in the gallery were recently shared by the tuner’s founder on social media, and they reveal the ride in question from multiple angles. This particular machine features a new grille at the front, with extra vents and some additional lights on the sides, as well as the tuner’s logo in the middle. Further down, we can clearly see that there are new bumper add-ons, including those around the side vents, and the ever-present splitter, which features blades on the sides in this case.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory Moreover, the pictured Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 also comes with an entirely new hood that has gone down the vented route. There is also new trim on the front fenders, and we can also see that the side steps appear to be new as well. The fender flares are part of the makeover, and so are the door mirror casings. Out back, the ride sports some add-ons on the sides of the bumper, a new roof-mounted spoiler, a fresh diffuser with an extra brake light in the middle, and new logos on the tailgate.
Some of the components mentioned above features a (forged-like) brown look, and the wheels, which are quite familiar, as the tuner has used them on numerous other projects recently, feature a bronze-like finish, and measure 24 inches in diameter. It seems that the SUV in question hasn’t had its suspension modified in any way, but you may want to refrain from quoting us on that for obvious reasons.
Don’t go anywhere yet, because we also have to put the spotlight on the interior. That’s because this Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 features custom leather upholstery that mixes black and brown. There are some very special inserts, including those on the seatbacks, and the Mansory emblems are ever present. The dashboard, center console, and door card trim is also new, and so is the steering wheel. A starry sky headliner is part of the makeover, as you can see in the pictures shared in our gallery.
Photo: Instagram | _kourosh_mansory Could a power boost be part of the makeover? Well, it certainly could, because Mansory tends to apply plenty of elbow grease to most of its projects. However, given that this aspect hasn’t been mentioned at all in the social media post embedded at the bottom of the page, we cannot tell you for sure whether this machine boasts more oomph or not. Our bet would be on the yes part, though that’s our two cents.
Even without any outside intervention whatsoever, the Mercedes-AMG GLS 63 is still very agile for a full-size SVU, taking 4.1 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill. Powering it is the ubiquitous 4.0-liter bi-turbo V8 engine, which is officially good for 603 hp (612 ps/450 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque.
The output and thrust has been retained in the facelifted iteration, which will go on sale soon in the United States of America. And that’s despite the fact that this model, as well as its smaller sibling, the GLE from AMG, benefit from a new integrated starter generator and a 48-volt mild-hybrid system, adding 23 hp (23 ps/17 kW) and 151 lb-ft (205 Nm) of torque. Both get the latest AMG Speedshift TCT 9-speed automatic transmission, channeling the power to the 4Matic+ AWD system with variable torque distribution.
Pricing will be released in due course, but the pre-facelifted iteration, which is what the pictured Mercedes- AMG GLS 63 is, kicked off at $151,050. Nonetheless, reports indicate that it should start at $155,250, before destination. But that does not matter in this story, as what does is whether you like the tuned machine or not. So, do you? For what it’s worth, I definitely don’t, but then again, I am not exactly a Mansory fan either. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Kourosh Mansory (@_kourosh_mansory)
